interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The postoperative pathology reveals a Gleason 4+3 (ISUP grade group 3) diagnosis with pathological stage pT3a. A key adverse finding is positive surgical margins, as noted by the surgical pathology report stating, "surgical margins were positive." Countervailing findings include the absence of extraprostatic extension and the absence of lymph node metastasis, with the report stating, "there was no lymph node metastasis." The seminal vesicles were not invaded, as documented by the surgical pathology report: "the seminal vesicles were not invaded."

The preoperative PSA level is not recorded, and postoperative PSA is also not recorded, meaning biochemical recurrence cannot be assessed. The nodal status is documented as "no lymph node metastasis," which is reassuring. The positive margins represent a significant adverse factor. Missing postoperative PSA and its trajectory significantly widen the uncertainty regarding biochemical recurrence. Information regarding postoperative PSA and its subsequent trajectory would be crucial in revising the prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 37.33 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 28.00–46.66 months; its coverage has not been validated.
